newsitem.title: USA: Biogen says Rentschler patent revoked.
newsitem.headline: Biogen says Rentschler patent revoked.

text.p: Biogen Inc said Wednesday that the Opposition Division of the European Patent Office (EPO) has revoked a patent issued to Dr Rentschler Biotechnologie GmbH and licensed to Schering AG relating to a specific cell line, production method, and form of recombinant beta interferon for multiple sclerosis.
Biogen said that the European Patent Office revoked the patent as a result of an opposition filed by Biogen.
According to Biogen, the Office ruled that the Rentschler patent was not valid on the grounds that the patent claims lacked novelty and inventive step.
On April 9, Biogen said that the EPO had revoked the patent for recombinant beta interferon licensed to Schering that covered a broader method of producing the compound.

"Although the revoked Rentschler patent did not cover (Biogen's) Avonex (Interferon beta-1a), we filed an opposition in order to remove uncertainty from the marketplace," said Jim Tobin, Biogen's President and Chief Executive Officer in a press release.
Rentschler has the opportunity to appeal the Opposition Division's decision to the EPO's Technical Board of Appeal, Biogen said.
